title: Feedback contrast and probe listing (jun 2026)
body:
Purpose: quick synthesis of recent customer feedback (May–Jun 2026) with contrasted asks, micro-vignettes, and a short list of low-effort probes we can run in the next 3 sprints. Aim is to make a tight set of experimentable changes product + infra can pick up at 1–3 engineer scope rather than large program bets.

High-level signal (one-liner): customers want clearer, predictable fallbacks when model latency or capacity causes degraded quality — many requests are small UX/contract changes + telemetry to reduce surprise.

Top themes (ranked by frequency & cost-to-fix):
1) Predictable fallback behavior and transparent routing: repeated asks for a deterministic explanation of how Redwood picks model variants when primary capacity is constrained (regional fallbacks, quantized variants). Customers want: deterministic mapping, observed latency bands per variant, and SLA implications.
2) Token-level cost visibility per route: more customers are instrumenting token costs to reconcile billing spikes. They request per-request token breakdown + quick CSV export.
3) Weaker responses from quantized/fast variants: product teams notice subtle hallucination drift when auto-fallback uses cheaper quantized variants. Customers want guardrails (confidence thresholds, soft-fallbacks).
4) Deployment isolation clarity for Dedicated vs Hosted: questions about burst policies and how they interact with reserved pools.
5) Developer ergonomics for retries and streaming: small but frequent asks for better SDK patterns and examples for reconnecting streaming sessions and resuming token streams.

Representative micro-vignettes (customer voice snippets):
- "We saw a 20% cost drop after enabling auto-fallback, but a handful of edge cases returned nonsense — need a way to mark a variant as 'read-only fallback' so it never becomes primary for critical routes." — large marketplace infra team.
- "Billing spiked on Friday when a scheduled test flooded our endpoint; we need per-request token CSVs to do root cause quickly." — fintech startup.
- "Region failover is great but we get different answer styles; can we pin style/temperature per-candidate variant?" — enterprise search provider.

Contrasted asks (what they asked vs what we currently do)
- Ask: per-request token breakdown + CSV export. Current: token breakdown exists in console aggregate but no single-request CSV. Gap: medium effort (backend + console UI).
- Ask: deterministic fallback mapping. Current: policy-based routing with opaque heuristics. Gap: docs + console exposure + small routing UI improvement.
- Ask: safe-fallback mode (quality-preserving). Current: model variants can be used as fallbacks without quality guardrails. Gap: runtime gating + toggle.

Quick probe hypotheses (small experiments we can do in 1–3 sprints):
Probe A — "Request-level cost dump" (owner: Marcus): add an opt-in parameter that returns a minimal token breakdown JSON for each request and a bulk export job in console. Hypothesis: reduces time-to-triage by >50% for billing incidents. Risk: extra logging cost.
Probe B — "Fallback transparency toggle" (owner: Product Eng): add a console switch to publish the fallback chain for a model route (primary -> variant list with latency bands). Hypothesis: reduces support tickets about 'why did you pick X' by 60%.
Probe C — "Soft-fallback validation" (owner: Applied ML): during fallback, run candidates in shadow and compute a quick semantic-similarity score; only allow fallback when score >= threshold. Hypothesis: reduces hallucination incidents by ~70% at modest throughput cost.
Probe D — "Streaming resume examples" (owner: DevX): ship 3 minimal SDK examples showing reconnect + resume logic for streaming and add them to quickstart. Hypothesis: reduces streaming-related bug reports by 40%.

Priority triage (simple rubric used here: customer impact x fix difficulty)
- P0 (high impact, low-to-medium effort): Request-level cost dump; Fallback transparency toggle; Streaming resume examples.
- P1 (high impact, higher effort): Soft-fallback validation (requires ML + runtime changes, measurable test plan).
- P2 (lower impact / research): Per-variant style pinning; Dedicated burst policy granularity (policy research + contract changes).

Dependencies & notes for eng/product: 
- Probe C (soft-fallback) needs a lightweight similarity endpoint (approx embedding + nearest-neighbor) that can run within SLOs. Might reuse Optimize team's embed cache.
- Token export needs a storage TTL policy and privacy review for logs. CS to coordinate with Security.

Suggested instrumentation additions (cheap wins):
- Annotate request logs with fallback_chain and variant_confidence tags.
- Add a synthetic probe job that hits routes with known answer sets and records a per-variant quality delta daily.
- Expose a CSV download button on per-route analytics page (limit: 7 days, 10k rows).

Immediate action items (next 2 weeks):
- Marcus: spike on request-level dump (prototype endpoint + proto CSV) — due 2026-06-26.
- Priya: open privacy ticket with Security for log retention/csv export — due 2026-06-19.
- Liam: draft console mock for fallback transparency toggle and landing copy — due 2026-06-22.
- Aisha: synthesize a one-page exec brief for product + infra outlining P0 list and expected headcount — due 2026-06-21.

Open questions / decisions needed: 
- Do we accept the extra cost of per-request token dumps for all customers, or gate behind a permission/paid tier? (Product decision)
- What threshold for shadow-similarity is acceptable operationally? (Applied ML + SRE)

Appendix: short checklist for customer communications
- For customers reporting hallucination after fallback: explain that we are trialing "soft-fallback" and request a small set of failing prompts for evaluation.
- For billing spikes: offer immediate ad-hoc CSV export and handoff to engineering for root cause.

Notes to self: this doc intentionally light on formal analysis — follow-up will produce a measurement plan for Probe C and cost estimates for token dump. Keep this as a living note; mark probes done/in-progress as we iterate.

End.
